title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: §7 of the 'Teichmülleries' notes. Grothendieck returns to maps after a group-theoretic computation (§6, eq. (100)) involving the groups pi^tau_{0,3}/<rho_1^2, rho_inf^n>. P is a 'poly-combinatoire', i.e. a polygon whose vertices carry weights (a 'pondération de type P'). Pi_P^tau is defined by presentation (62), which does not appear on this page. It is presumably the polygonal reflection (Coxeter) group: one involution tau_a per edge a of P, with (tau_a tau_b)^{n_v}=1 when edges a and b meet at a vertex v of weight n_v. The previous page fits this reading: rho_1 = tau_0 tau_inf, with relations rho_1^2 and rho_inf^n. In orbifold terms, Pi_P^tau is the orbifold fundamental group of P viewed as a reflection orbifold with corner angles pi/n_v.

Theorem stated on this page (eq. (101)): the functor X -> R(X) is an equivalence of categories between
- finite P-weighted maps X (cellular decompositions of compact surfaces whose faces are copies of P, edges carrying types, considered up to isotopy), and
- finite Pi_P^tau-sets on which every tau_a acts without fixed points.
Here R(X) is the set of faces, and tau_a sends a face to its neighbour across that face's edge of type a. Figure: a square face Gamma with its four neighbours tau_0Gamma, ..., tau_3Gamma; edge labels appear in reversed cyclic order on the neighbours, showing that the tau_a reverse orientation. The fixed-point-free condition excludes boundary or folded edges.

Oriented version (eq. (102)): Pi_P is the index-2 rotation subgroup, the kernel of Pi_P^tau -> {±1} with tau -> -1 (eq. (103), next page). Finite oriented P-weighted maps are equivalent to finite Pi_P-sets via X -> R^+(X), the set of 'direct' faces, i.e. faces whose orientation induced by X agrees with the cyclic order on the vertices (or edges) of P fixed by a chosen orientation omega. No freeness condition is needed here. Inducing up, Pi_P^tau x_{Pi_P} E, automatically makes tau act freely, since tau swaps the two cosets.

Next page: a quasi-inverse comes from Galois theory of covers. Finite Pi_P-sets correspond to finite ramified covers of the sphere Sigma_P (the double of P) that are étale over Sigma_P^*, the sphere with the vertices removed. The equivalence is realised by pulling back the canonical (universal) oriented P-weighted map on Sigma_P.

Purpose: generalise the cartographic group / dessins dictionary (Esquisse) from triangles, i.e. triangle groups and maps/hypermaps, to arbitrary weighted polygons. The aim is a combinatorial description of covers of Sigma_P^*, linked to the Teichmüller tower and Galois actions.
errors: No real error. One point is left implicit: since (tau_a tau_b)^{n_v}=1, the valency of a vertex of type v in X divides n_v rather than equalling it. So 'P-weighted map' must allow vertex orders dividing the weight, or the weights act as upper bounds in the divisibility sense.
'Endomorphismes involutifs' should be 'automorphismes involutifs'. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Group generated by involutions indexed by the edges of a weighted polygon, with dihedral relations at the vertices (Pi_P^tau), and its orientation subgroup Pi_P
ideas.modern_name: Polygonal Coxeter group / extended polygon group (orbifold pi_1 of a reflection polygon) and its rotation subgroup
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartographic groups and their higher or 'polyhedral' variants, but not in this polygonal form

ideas.what: Equivalence: finite P-weighted maps <-> finite Pi_P^tau-sets with fixed-point-free tau_a (faces as elements, reflections across edges)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial maps with P-gonal faces <-> permutation representations; thin chamber systems of cyclic Coxeter type
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (1978) for triangle groups/maps; Tits (1981) chamber systems; Vince, Lins (early 1980s) for colored-graph encodings of maps
ideas.where_published: The triangle case is in the Esquisse d'un programme (cartographic groups C_2, C_2^+)

ideas.what: Oriented version via 'direct' faces R^+(X), and its dependence on a choice of orientation of P
ideas.modern_name: Orientation double cover / rotation subgroup correspondence for oriented maps

missed.claim: The fixed-point-free Pi_P^tau-sets are exactly thin chamber systems over the edge set of P, with Coxeter diagram the cycle of P labelled by the vertex weights. Grothendieck's P-weighted maps are thus Tits-style chamber systems or 'thin geometries' of polygonal Coxeter type, written down in 1981 in parallel to Tits's 'A local approach to buildings'. The link from dessins/Teichmüller towers to chamber systems is only implicit in the later literature.
missed.quote: les ensembles finis où opère Π_P^τ — i.e. munis d'endomorphismes involutifs τ_a, indexés par les arêtes de P — s'interprètent en termes de telles cartes, mais en supposant que les τ_a opèrent sans points fixes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests treating the Galois action on polygonal dessins (covers of spheres with weighted punctures) through Coxeter/chamber-system combinatorics. Mostly, though, this is a reformulation of known material.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct generalisation of the map/cartographic-group dictionary from triangles to weighted polygons. It is essentially standard: Coxeter polygon groups acting on face sets, with the orientation subgroup giving oriented maps. It is a nice unpublished detail of Grothendieck's program but contains no result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The phrase around 'dont il symétrise par' should read roughly: 'un ensemble où opèrent des opérations τ_a, où τ_a correspond à la symétrie par rapport à l'arête de type a d'une face'.
'(101)' under the figure labels the equivalence of categories, as the next page refers to 'l'équivalence (101)', not just the figure.
'(cat. topologiques)' may rather be '(cat. isotopiques)', i.e. maps up to isotopy. The handwriting is unclear.
In the margin: 'Une pondération de type P', glossing 'carte X P-pondérée'.

'(disons, numérotation circulaire) des [orbites d'une] faces' is uncertain. The inserted words appear to be 'orbites d'une' above a struck-out word, and the sense is that the face labelling is induced by that of the vertices.
Over 'correspond' the insertion is 'où τ_a', replacing the struck-out 'correspond...'.
